subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 3-year-old girl had normal development until 14 months of age, when she began to regress in motor, verbal, and cognitive skills. She now has stereotypic hand-wringing, ataxia, and seizures, and her head growth has slowed. Genetic testing shows a de novo mutation in MECP2.
question: The protein encoded by this gene normally contributes to gene silencing by which mechanism?

options.text: Binding methylated CpG dinucleotides and recruiting transcriptional repression.
Cleaving target mRNAs within the RNA-induced silencing complex.
Acetylating histone tails to open chromatin and activate transcription.
Removing introns from pre-mRNA as part of the spliceosome.
Phosphorylating RNA polymerase II to initiate transcription.

explanation_correct: MECP2 encodes methyl-CpG-binding protein 2, which recognizes methylated cytosine residues in DNA and helps recruit repressive complexes that silence transcription. Loss-of-function mutations cause Rett syndrome, a de novo X-linked dominant disorder that is seen mostly in females and is embryonically lethal in males.

explanation_incorrect.B: mRNA cleavage in the RNA-induced silencing complex is carried out by Argonaute proteins loaded with siRNA, not by MECP2.
explanation_incorrect.C: Histone acetylation by histone acetyltransferases opens chromatin and activates transcription; MECP2 is associated with repression.
explanation_incorrect.D: Introns are removed by the spliceosome; MECP2 acts on methylated DNA to regulate transcription.
explanation_incorrect.E: Phosphorylation of RNA polymerase II is part of transcription initiation and elongation and is not the function of a methyl-CpG-binding protein.

educationalObjective: MECP2 encodes a methyl-CpG-binding protein that helps silence methylated DNA, and its loss of function causes Rett syndrome.
